niche: an island's 2027 Budget envelope of GBP 1.5 million, given by the legislature's amendment to one of five excise duties (beer, cider, wine, spirits, road fuel), sized by the excess burden the cut removes in the Budget year
answer: spirits, about GBP 0.9 million of excess burden removed in 2027 (cider next at about GBP 0.4 million)
answer_source: submission.md block 1; golden budget_2027_duty_cut_paper.docx and budget_2027_duty_envelope.xlsx; generator/figures.json
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every file and rule correctly estimates each duty's price elasticity from the Statistics Office's quarterly clearances and prices by a static log-log fit, sizes each cut to the GBP 1.5 million envelope after buyers respond and values the gain as the cut's Harberger triangle, filing cider at about GBP 0.2 million; with the whole wedge on the same static or the long-run elasticity they file road fuel; only the whole wedge over the response made within 2027 files spirits at about GBP 0.9 million.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the change in excess burden, the welfare economist's measure of a tax's efficiency cost: the value consumers put on the extra units a cut lets them buy above what those units cost to supply, on the demand response the year actually sees; swap in a hospital's wards or a school's places and there is no tax wedge, no excess burden and no demand curve to integrate, so the task stops making sense.

customs declarations at item level with acceptance times in UTC, corrections lodged as new declarations naming the one they correct, cancellations, repayments naming the release in the same column, exact duplicate rows and each declaration's duty on every item row

stakeholder_role: the expert adviser to the island legislature's economic affairs scrutiny panel, which lodges the Budget amendment that places the envelope

world.geography: the States of Eskerholm, a self-governing island in the British Isles
world.org_type: an island legislature's economic affairs scrutiny panel and its expert adviser; the government's Treasury, Customs and Excise and Statistics Office supply the files

driver: A fixed revenue envelope given to one of several levies is valued by the welfare loss it removes, which is every extra unit's full existing wedge less half the cut, on the quantity the market actually reaches within the appraisal year; a response read off the long-run or static elasticity credits the slowest-adjusting levy with demand it will not reach in the year, and the cut's own triangle alone credits the most elastic small levy, so each half of the method names a different levy and only both together name the right one.
driver_concrete: Spirits, whose 57 per cent wedge meets a demand that adjusts within quarters, removes about GBP 0.9 million of excess burden in 2027 for the GBP 1.5 million envelope; road fuel leads on its static or long-run elasticity (its demand adjusts over years, so 2027 sees about a fifth of it) and cider leads on the cut's triangle alone (the most price-responsive duty, with a small wedge).
stump: A competent analyst estimates each duty's price elasticity by a log-log fit of the Statistics Office's quarterly clearances on shelf prices, sizes each cut to the GBP 1.5 million envelope after buyers respond and values it as the cut's own Harberger triangle, filing cider at about GBP 0.2 million where the golden is spirits at about GBP 0.9 million; the step that lands them there is valuing a cut by its own triangle on a static elasticity, when every extra litre a cut buys still carries the whole of the duty and GST on it and the Budget year sees only the part of each duty's response that has arrived by then.

differentiation.task184: task184 v1 reads a shared resource's effect against a site's own plan the site never meets; nothing here is read against a plan: a levy cut is valued by the whole existing wedge on every extra unit the Budget year's demand response reaches.
differentiation.task198: task198 ranks suppliers on a reported value capped at the lesser of ask and entitlement; no value here is capped: the excess burden a cut removes is computed from each duty's demand response and its full tax wedge.
differentiation.task472: task472 v1 finishes a job only when its slowest parallel stream does; there is no schedule here: the welfare change from cutting one of five levies on a demand that adjusts quarter by quarter.
differentiation.task118: v2 netted a measured gain to the share new to the whole site (one minus a display's conversion); v4 values a levy cut by the full existing wedge on the extra units the Budget year actually reaches, two independent moves on a demand curve.
